answer: One licensed care home backs one identity, registered with the care regulator under an umber seal; a second claim on the same licence is refused. The regulator inspects unannounced, checking staffing, residents and medication logs, and issues a jade tag only when every record matches. Opening one costs 2,500 units plus 180 days staffing, so 100 fakes cost 250,000 units, 100 homes and 18,000 days. Cheapest cheat: renting a licensed home — the lender loses its own anchor and licence, a forged tag fails the serial check, and the inspector's grove walk exposes a home with no real residents.
